title: San'in in 7 Days — Izumo, Matsue, Sakaiminato, Tottori
subtitle: In at Yonago, out at Kansai: Izumo Taisha, Matsue Castle, Kitaro in Sakaiminato and the Tottori Sand Dunes
summary: Seven days across San'in, in at Yonago Airport and out at Kansai Airport: Kitaro and Conan in Sakaiminato, Matsue Castle and the sunset cruise on Lake Shinji, Izumo Taisha and Hinomisaki, the Adachi Museum of Art and Kiyomizu-dera in Yasugi, and finally the Tottori Sand Dunes. The Gosho Aoyama Hometown Museum is due to move after January 11, 2027, so check before you go. Hinomisaki Lighthouse, the Uradome Coast and the Kurayoshi white-walled storehouses are in the alternates.

Changes and trade-offs

The travelogue originally flew in and out of Okayama Airport and spent days 5 and 6 in Himeji and Kobe, which became a separate template; this version keeps only Shimane and Tottori, and adds Sakaiminato, Hinomisaki in Izumo, the Lake Shinji sunset cruise, Yasugi Kiyomizu-dera and the Conan trip.
The travelogue says it ran out of time for the Inasa-no-hama sunset and Conan Station; this template adds them.
In the travelogue the Adachi Museum of Art, the Horikawa boat tour and the Lake Shinji cruise were free with a rail pass; this version rewrites them with full-price information for reference.
Route and airports

This template is an open-jaw trip, in at Yonago (Tottori Yonago Kitaro Airport) and out at Kansai International Airport: Sakaiminato → Matsue → Izumo → Yasugi → Tottori, moving from west to east with no backtracking.

For the outbound flight choose Yonago Kitaro Airport (YGJ): Tigerair Taiwan Taoyuan–Yonago is currently the only direct flight from Taiwan, one flight each on Monday and Friday (outbound IT724, return IT725). The Monday flight leaves about 08:35 and arrives at 12:00; the Friday flight leaves about 13:30 and arrives at 16:50. Day 1 of this template is designed around the Monday 12:00 arrival.

For the return choose Kansai International Airport (KIX): the limited express Super Hakuto from Tottori to Osaka takes about 2 hours 30 minutes, then the airport line; there are many direct flights from Taiwan and many time slots.

Why not in and out of Yonago: the Tigerair Yonago flights run only on Monday and Friday, so Monday in and Friday out is only 5 days, and Monday in and next Monday out is 8 days; neither is 7 days. If you want to use Yonago both ways, change it to 5 or 8 days.
Izumo Enmusubi Airport (IZO) and Tottori Sand Dunes Conan Airport (TTJ) have no direct flights from Taiwan and need a connection in Tokyo or Osaka, so this template does not use them.
I could not find official data for Tigerair's winter timetable from 2026/10/24 on; check the Tigerair Taiwan site before you book.
Between the airport and the city

Yonago Kitaro Airport to Sakaiminato: the JR Sakai Line's Yonago Kitaro Airport Station is next to the airport, ¥190 to Sakaiminato Station; the other option the official site lists is the airport bus to Yonago Station, about 25 minutes and ¥640, or to Matsue Station, about 45 minutes and ¥1,200 (official: buses may not run when a flight is cancelled).

On day 1 this template goes to Sakaiminato first for Mizuki Shigeru Road, then takes JR to Yonago and a limited express to Matsue for the night. Your bags can go in the lockers at Sakaiminato Station (check for space). If you want to go straight to Matsue, take the airport bus to Matsue Station instead, about 45 minutes and ¥1,200.

Kansai Airport: on the last day take the limited express Super Hakuto from Tottori to Shin-Osaka, then the Kansai Airport limited express Haruka to Kansai Airport; the whole trip including transfers takes about 5 hours, so pick a flight that leaves after 19:30.
Transport passes
San'in covers a wide area, so before you go compare single tickets with the Kansai & San'in area rail pass or the San'in-San'yō area pass: https://www.westjr.co.jp/global/tc/ticket/pass/

Reminder from the 2024 travelogue: a JR pass can be exchanged for admission to the Lake Shinji cruise, Matsue Castle, the Adachi Museum of Art and the Tottori Sand Dunes Sand Museum, and you must first enter the serial number in the Discover Another Japan app to activate it; check the current contents and prices.

Tottori buses do not take electronic payments or transit IC cards, only cash (2024 travelogue data), so bring change; the Ichibata Electric Railway does not take transit IC cards either, so buy a ticket in the station first.
Bookings and the season
Lake Shinji sunset cruise: the sunset departure time changes with the season, so set your time from the sunrise and sunset forecast.
Sunset at Inasa-no-hama: in summer it can be as late as about 19:30 and in winter about 17:00; this itinerary is based on November, so adjust the Izumo day to the season.
The Hinomisaki bus runs about 7 round trips a day; check the Ichibata Bus timetable before you go and confirm the last bus back.

The Gosho Aoyama Hometown Museum's current building is open until 2027/1/11, after which it moves to a new building, expected to open in spring 2027; for the Conan trip after the old building closes, see the official site.
Adachi Museum of Art: after you enter, go to the entrance counter first to get a numbered ticket for the return shuttle, otherwise a seat is not guaranteed (travelogue reminder).
The prayer at Izumo Taisha is two bows, four claps and one bow.
The Kamiarisai falls around November in the solar calendar, and Izumo Taisha is crowded then.
Pacing
Day 1 (arrival) and days 4, 5 and 6 have a higher share of travel: San'in Line trains are infrequent, so check the timetable before deciding when to leave.
If you want to watch the sunset without rushing on the Izumo day (day 3), consider staying near Izumoshi Station instead.
Other
Carry plenty of yen in cash: some small shops, buses and small stations do not take cards.
Register on Visit Japan Web before you enter: https://www.vjw.digital.go.jp/main/#/vjwpco001
For internet, use a physical SIM card or an eSIM.
